stances_toward.note: Constitutionally a federal region, de facto an autonomous government with its own Peshmerga, oil contracts and foreign contacts, so own_territory here means controlled and claimed with limits, not administered by Baghdad. The tension is fiscal and military: Kurdish exports via Ceyhan stopped in March 2023 (an estimated USD 35bn of lost revenue), resumed on 27 September 2025 with all sales through SOMO, were suspended again at the start of the Iran war and restarted under the 17 March 2026 deal (up to 450,000 b/d including 250,000 b/d from Kirkuk); budget transfers are leverage in the disputes over oil, territory and Peshmerga status. Erbil took most of the Iranian fire (about 1,000 missiles and drones) and its prime minister called the US withdrawal without air defences 'shameful'. Bond - kin: one state, one constitution, a decades-long quarrel inside it.

stances_toward.note: The KDP has competed with the PYD for a generation (it backs the Kurdish National Council and, per the PKK's own May 2025 congress statement, kept an 'embargo' on the PKK), but the Abdi-Masoud Barzani meeting in Erbil on 16 Jan 2025, the Qamishli unity conference (26 Apr 2025, a Barzani envoy attending) and Barzani's role in January 2026 (consulted before the 16 Jan withdrawal, host of the 17 and 22 Jan meetings with Barrack and CENTCOM, offered as a guarantor) made Erbil the SDF's most useful Kurdish partner; Nechirvan Barzani invited al-Sharaa to Erbil on 3 Aug 2026. Partner, warming, not ally: Erbil is a mediator with its own agenda (and a PUK that condemned the attack more strongly). The KDP-PKK split is the structural fault: the SDF's PKK-lineage cadre sits between them. Bond - kin.
